parts.title: The Wilted Bean Plant
parts.text: Maya arrived at the science fair early, eager to present her bean-plant experiment. But one plant had drooped overnight while its neighbors stood tall, an **anomaly** that made no sense. Her teacher offered only a **vague** explanation: "Maybe it got too much light." Maya wanted something **tangible**, a clue she could hold, not guesses. Then her friend Ethan whispered that a jealous competitor might **sabotage** a project to win.

parts.title: Searching for Clues
parts.text: Ethan, who loved logic, insisted they follow a **rigid** plan: check every table, record every detail, and accept nothing without proof. Near Maya's display they found only a **meager** pile of evidence, one smudged fingerprint and a torn scrap of paper. Priya, the fair's photographer, pointed to the window latch beside the display. "It looks like someone tried to **tamper** with it," she said. Before accusing anyone, they agreed to **verify** each detail against the school's security records.

parts.title: The Truth Comes Out
parts.text: As the day went on, the mystery began to **unravel**. Several classmates met the sabotage theory with **scorn**, laughing that nobody would attack a bean plant. Then Mr. Webb, the custodian, explained that a broken heater had forced him to **curtail** his evening rounds and pry the stuck window open to air out the room. His story was **plausible**, and the security log matched it. The cold night draft had reached only Maya's plant.

parts.title: What the Plant Taught Them
parts.text: By closing time, Maya had rewritten her poster to include the cold-draft discovery. She realized that a good scientist follows evidence instead of suspicion. The judges awarded the trio a ribbon for the best investigation, and the drooping bean plant became the star of the fair.

definitions.meaning1: Not clear or specific; hard to understand or describe exactly. Example: The map gave only vague directions, so we kept getting lost.
definitions.studentChallenge: Her ___ answer left us unsure what she really meant.

definitions.meaning1: Real enough to be touched or measured, not just an idea. Example: The trophy was tangible proof of the team's hard work.
definitions.meaning2: Clear and definite enough to be seen as real. Example: The new playground brought tangible benefits to the neighborhood.
definitions.studentChallenge: A hug is a feeling, but a gift is something ___ you can hold.

definitions.meaning1: Stiff and not easily bent. Example: The rigid plastic ruler snapped when he tried to bend it.
definitions.meaning2: Strict and unwilling to change. Example: The coach's rigid schedule left no room for surprises.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ steel beam did not bend, even under heavy weight.

definitions.meaning1: To damage or ruin something on purpose to keep it from working or succeeding. Example: A jealous rival tried to sabotage the robot before the contest.
definitions.meaning2: The act of deliberately damaging or ruining something. Example: Investigators suspected sabotage when every machine in the factory stopped at once.
definitions.studentChallenge: The spy hoped to ___ the rocket launch by cutting its power.

definitions.meaning1: To meddle with something in a way that damages or changes it without permission. Example: It is against the law to tamper with someone else's mail.
definitions.studentChallenge: Please do not ___ with the experiment while it is running.

definitions.meaning1: Something that is different from what is normal or expected. Example: A warm, sunny day in the middle of January was a strange anomaly.
definitions.studentChallenge: Snow in the desert would be a strange ___ that scientists would study for years.

definitions.meaning1: To cut short or reduce. Example: The storm forced the town to curtail its summer festival.
definitions.studentChallenge: Budget cuts may ___ the school's after-school clubs.

definitions.meaning1: Very small in amount or quality; not enough. Example: A meager meal of broth and bread barely filled the hikers.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ paycheck was hardly enough to buy groceries.

definitions.meaning1: To check that something is true or correct. Example: Please verify the spelling in a dictionary before you turn in your essay.
definitions.studentChallenge: The reporter called two sources to ___ the story before printing it.

definitions.meaning1: A strong feeling that someone or something is worthless or foolish. Example: She looked at the cheater's excuse with scorn.
definitions.meaning2: To treat as worthless or to reject with contempt. Example: Some people scorn advice they do not want to hear.
definitions.studentChallenge: The princess looked at the flattering liar with ___ and walked away.

definitions.meaning1: To come apart, as threads do; to undo something that was tied or woven. Example: The old sweater began to unravel at the cuff.
definitions.meaning2: To solve or become clear, as a mystery or plot. Example: The detective worked all night to unravel the mystery.
definitions.studentChallenge: If you keep pulling that loose thread, the whole sleeve will ___.

definitions.meaning1: Seeming reasonable and likely to be true. Example: It was plausible that the bus was late because of the heavy snow.
definitions.studentChallenge: Getting stuck in traffic was a ___ reason for being late.

Dara did not want to accuse anyone without proof, so she decided to _(3)_ every detail first. Someone had tried to _(4)_ with the lock, leaving fresh scratches. Mr. Hale, who followed a _(5)_ rule that nobody entered the lab alone, shook his head, and a few students greeted Dara's worries with _(6)_.

She wanted something _(7)_, such as a photo or a fingerprint, not just a feeling. The hallway camera showed a student whose key had stuck in the lock, a story that was entirely _(8)_. He had never meant to _(9)_ the project; he had come to finish his work.

Budget cuts forced the club to _(10)_ its weekend hours, and it had only _(11)_ supplies left. Still, Dara felt proud that she had managed to _(12)_ the puzzle without blaming the wrong person.
